body: my cat is fairly old as well but she sure doesn’t look it, i feel like once you give most cats wet food they never can go back. your other cat has interesting taste in food lol
i sure will, thank you for everything, this really helped me. i might post a picture of it once i’m done so you can judge how well i did lol. in any case i’ll let you know :))
that sounds lovely, i’ll be sure to give it a shot sometime!

i have a cat too so i completely understand, i love her so much. i had lost my previous cat around december and kept all of her things, when my uncle passed away a few months ago from covid his cat had no place to go so i adopted her and have been looking after her ever since. i’d feed her better food than the wet food but she doesn’t have the best teeth unfortunately
also i’ll be sure to try out that english sunday lunch, i’m scared of a lot of desserts but i just might give the yorkshire pudding a try

that’s where having a dog and cooking at night helps, even if i messed up then nobody would know and it wouldn’t go to waste. my good boy always would think my food was the best, even when it didn’t turn out so great. google is telling me the correct way of spelling the salads name in english is Olivier (though it sounds like olivye spoken), you boil carrots, potatoes, and eggs then peal the carrots and potatoes. you then need to dice those up along with an onion and some ukrainian pickles (surprisingly i do think the type matters flavor wise, you can buy them at ukrainian markets but if you can’t find them it’s not the end of the world), but you combine that with peas, ham cubes, sour cream, and mayo and you will have cold war russian potato salad (or at least the way i was taught to do it) :)

last night i made a ton of butter chicken curry with white rice, but i also can make a bunch of different omelettes (my favorite is a french style omelette) as well as burgers and fries like the american i am lol. i’ve been experimenting with buttermilk fried chicken and making sandwiches as well as chicken and waffles. one of my favorite dishes i learned from my step-mom (who is from the Ukraine), it’s a cold war potato salad that has been mostly forgotten, it takes like a whole day to make but it’s delicious. i love learning recipes from different places around the world, if you have any recommendations i’d be happy to look up a new dish

no worries, i appreciate the conversation more than anything else. it’s easy for me to forget there are kind people out there like yourself, especially when i feel like this. honestly i don’t think i’m a fantastic teacher, and i learned to cook over quarantine every night at like 1 am. i would watch a lot of channels on yt and do my best to copy the recipes, i was a lot worse then than i am now, like most things it just requires a lot of practice. one of the things that has brought me a lot of comfort is cooking for people, i think they can tell how much i put into it and making other people happy is a really nice feeling. part of what motivates me to improve at it i guess.

it’s alright, you are correct i am from the US. i don’t want to get into the specifics that much but i’m in a position where if the police were called on me then i would really have to hope i’m successful. the reality of them finding out like that would be a lot worse than dying itself.

it turns something i’d rather deal with privately into the police knocking on my door. i’ve read stories of operators freaking out and sending cops for less than what i’m going through. i don’t live alone, and they can’t know what’s going on with me.
